items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: I got to know Charlie Watts pretty well, a big jazz fan.

ctx.x: I didn’t write that. It was such a smaller scene back then. Like if you say the Rolling Stones now what you picture is a billion dollar organization going around the world in

trucks and planes and stuff. But back, this was 1967, 1968 — I mean they were well known, they had some hit records, but there was a scene — this one particular recording studio, it was called Olympic Studios, it was outside of London. I went to school in Brighton, which was a one hour train ride up to London. And while I was in graduate school friends of mine from San Francisco had come over to England, they had been signed to Capitol Records and they were going to make their first record in England. And so I…

How did they present the Stones or these other folks you worked with, how did they present the songs to you? Did they have a chord chart or they said here’s how it goes, sit next to you with their guitars and you just learned it that way then played your part?
